findings.title: 10 crates silently opt out of the workspace-wide clippy -D warnings gate via undocumented crate-level allow(clippy::all, dead_code)
findings.description: Crate-level #![allow(clippy::all, dead_code, unused_imports, mismatched_lifetime_syntaxes)] in buff-lsp, buff-mcp, buff-geo, buff-game, buff-auth, buff-db, buff-email, buff-config, buff-scrape, buff-image (all at src/lib.rs line 1). CI runs 'cargo clippy $CI_CRATES --all-targets -- -D warnings' over the FULL workspace (since ITER-32), so these 10 crates are effectively exempt from every clippy lint plus dead-code detection. No rationale comment accompanies the allows, and no AGENTS.md documents them; contrast the documented per-crate #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)] which always carries inline justification.
findings.root_cause: Copy-pasted scaffold header propagated across crates (2 tooling + 8 framework), likely committed from a local-dev state where lints were suppressed to unblock iteration; never revisited during the v1.24/v1.26 hygiene waves.
findings.impact: Real lint violations and dead code accumulate invisibly in 10/73 crates; the architectural invariant 'one uniform quality gate across the workspace' is eroded; future refactors of these crates get no clippy safety net; inconsistent enforcement misleads contributors about actual code health.
findings.recommendation: Delete allow(clippy::all) from all 10 crates, run clippy per crate, fix or individually justify surviving lints with targeted inline allows carrying rationale comments (matching the result_large_err precedent). If triage is large for a crate, allow only specific lint groups temporarily with a tracking comment.

Verify via Select-String sweep that zero allow(clippy::all remains workspace-wide

findings.title: Lexer publicly exports indent/string_interp internals that have zero cross-crate consumers
findings.description: buff-lang-lexer/src/lib.rs declares 'pub mod indent;' and 'pub mod string_interp;' (lines 20, 22), exposing the offside-rule indent tracker and string-interpolation scanner as public API. A workspace-wide grep for buff_lang_lexer::(indent|string_interp) finds zero consumers outside the lexer crate itself; the crate's own AGENTS.md documents the public surface as only 'tokenize, Token, TokenKind, LexerError'. The parser consumes Indent/Dedent tokens purely via the tokenize() stream, never the tracker directly.
findings.root_cause: lib.rs uses blanket 'pub mod' for all five modules rather than restricting internal machinery to pub(crate); the module docs were written for the narrower intended surface and never reconciled with the actual exports.
findings.impact: Offside-rule algorithm internals (ITER-36 dedent invariants) and interpolation scanning become de-facto public API: any external/crate consumer could start depending on them, turning internal-algorithm changes into breaking API changes and widening the lexer's blast radius beyond its designed 'tokenize' seam.
findings.recommendation: Demote both modules: 'pub(crate) mod indent;' and 'pub(crate) mod string_interp;' (keep 'pub mod token/lexer/error'), re-run cargo check/test for the lexer, parser, and workspace to confirm no hidden consumer exists, and update the per-crate AGENTS.md public-API list if it diverges further.
fix_guide: Change the two pub mod declarations to pub(crate) mod
Run cargo check --workspace and cargo test -p buff-lang-lexer -p buff-lang-parser
If a consumer surfaces, evaluate it explicitly instead of keeping the export
Update crates/buff-lang-lexer/AGENTS.md public-surface line if needed
findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path crates\buff-lang-lexer\src\lib.rs -Pattern 'pub mod'; Get-ChildItem crates -Recurse -Filter *.rs | Select-String -Pattern 'buff_lang_lexer::(indent|string_interp)'

confidence.rationale: Zero-consumer claim rests on a full-workspace grep of .rs files; doc-vs-code divergence verified by direct read; small residual risk that a macro-generated path or re-export chain references the modules without the literal prefix

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Pure API-surface observation, no behavior claim; FP only if some consumer exists outside literal-grep reach (unlikely in this repo's import style)

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md dependency-exception inventory omits four verified production edges
findings.description: ARCHITECTURE.md line 157-160 asserts the framework group has 'exactly three intra-framework edges ... plus buff-plugins', and lines 171-189 present a four-item 'Known exceptions, all deliberate and documented' list presented as complete. Manifest-verified production edges missing from the inventory: buff-mock -> buff-lang-ast (crates/buff-mock/Cargo.toml:36), buff-fuzz -> buff-lang-ast (crates/buff-fuzz/Cargo.toml:44), buff-pipeline -> buff-lang-runtime (crates/buff-pipeline/Cargo.toml:34), and tooling edge buff-mcp -> buff-lsp (crates/buff-mcp/Cargo.toml:26). Each edge IS documented in its own crate manifest/AGENTS.md; the gap is in the authoritative structural doc only.
findings.root_cause: ARCHITECTURE.md's exception list was curated around compiler-crate layering exceptions; framework->compiler-core helper edges (T25/T27 codegen-helper pattern) and the mcp->lsp pairing were added in later waves without folding them into the central inventory.
findings.impact: Readers treat the four-item list as the complete deviation set; future audits and 'cargo tree' reviews will flag the four edges as undocumented violations, and the 'exactly three intra-framework edges' claim invites false confidence about framework coupling.
findings.recommendation: Extend the Known-exceptions list with the four edges (one line each, citing the manifest line), and reword the framework-group paragraph to 'three intra-framework edges plus three framework->compiler-core helper edges (mock->ast, fuzz->ast, pipeline->runtime) all following the T25/T27 codegen-helper pattern'.

findings.title: Leaf-crate convention 'ZERO internal deps â€” only thiserror' contradicted by T1-sanctioned serde/serde_json
findings.description: crates/buff-lang-error/AGENTS.md line 29 states the convention 'ZERO internal deps â€” only thiserror ... do not add crate deps without strong reason', while the crate manifest ([dependencies] lines 16-17) carries serde + serde_json, added in v1.25 T1 (JSON diagnostic output) with inline manifest documentation calling them 'the only non-thiserror deps on this leaf crate â€” explicitly sanctioned'. The manifest is self-consistent; the AGENTS.md convention line was never updated, so the leaf crate's guardrail now reads as permanently violated.
findings.root_cause: T1 added serde/serde_json with rationale documented in Cargo.toml comments but did not amend the per-crate AGENTS.md CONVENTIONS block, leaving doc and manifest in direct contradiction on the workspace's most depended-on crate (22 dependents).
findings.impact: Agents auditing or extending the leaf crate get contradictory guardrails: either they 'restore' the convention by removing sanctioned deps (breaking buff check --error-format json), or they learn AGENTS.md guardrails are advisory, weakening all other leaf-crate rules.
findings.recommendation: Update the convention line to 'External deps: thiserror + serde/serde_json (T1 JSON diagnostics, manifest-documented). ZERO internal workspace deps â€” this is the foundation; do not add crate deps without strong reason + inline manifest rationale.' This preserves the real invariant (no internal edges) while matching the manifest.

fix_examples.after:
- **ZERO internal workspace deps**. External deps: `thiserror` + `serde`/`serde_json`
  (T1 JSON diagnostic output â€” rationale inline in Cargo.toml). Do not add deps
  without strong reason documented inline in the manifest.
